scope: Root requested independent code-only review; outputs confined to publication_root_preparation/V196_ARCHITECTURE_CODE_REVIEW_B.

code_facts.q_conditioning: Original crop is centered at original q; relative XY is identical across rows; original numeric q/L/native and endpoint location are not forward tensors.
code_facts.normalization: GroupNorm per convolution; no BatchNorm or dropout
code_facts.outputs: support Linear64->2, owner Linear64->3, separate direct_end Linear64->1, all sharing encoder/pool/shared64
code_facts.objective: Mean of old five losses on192 rows plus balanced direct BCE on32 rows (16D+16E), weight1.
code_facts.direct_decode: Finite available raw>=0 -> E; raw<0 -> D; original unavailable/nonfinite -> U; separate support/owner/proxy outputs.

root_reported_metadata_not_remeasured.authority: Root message; saved V196 metadata observation, not opened or independently remeasured in this review.
root_reported_metadata_not_remeasured.quantity_distinction: Continuous enclosure extent and positive fourtap sample participation have different definitions; neither is a count of exact semantic end pixels.

code_consistent_hypotheses_not_establish: A small spatially varying end cue can be mixed with surrounding context by strided convolution, average pooling and shared feature compression.
The network must infer which endpoint is intended from the q-centered image and constant coordinates; no explicit endpoint offset/native identity is supplied.
Broad support, ownership and whole-object SAM mask can encode a different target from queried-end visibility; their causal help, harm or gradient interference has not been measured.
countervailing_facts: Convolution may encode small cues before downsampling; code alone cannot prove cue destruction.
The final3x3 bins and constant XY retain coarse position information; this is not spatially invariant1x1 global pooling.
GroupNorm has spatial coupling, so convolution-only receptive-field arithmetic would not be a strict effective dependency boundary.
not_measured: Learned activations, saliency, gradients, effective receptive field or checkpoint behavior.
End-local RGB delta magnitude/contrast/noise or observer-level visibility and target-identification reliability.
Causal effect of pooling, SAM, shared losses or localization on source or real generalization.
Confidence calibration or whether zero abstentions imply solved uncertainty.
limitations: Static code supports possible mechanisms only. Root-reported saved geometry/byte-change facts do not establish learned-feature loss, semantic correctness, learnability, or real transfer.
